newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia readies concessions for Trans-Yugo highways.
newsitem.headline: Serbia readies concessions for Trans-Yugo highways.

text.p: Serbia is readying a new law on concessions for road building within trans-Yugoslav highways project and the most successful bidders will be chosen by the end of 1997, a senior government official said on Tuesday.
"The Construction Ministry has prepared a new law on concessions to be adopted in the parliament in April at the latest," Transportation Minister Svetolik Kostadinovic told Reuters in an interview.
The law sets criteria and conditions for getting concessions for road building, equally for foreign and domestic companies, the minister said.

"The government has also set up a special commission of representatives from the ministries of construction, finance and transportation, charged with preparing (international) tenders and choosing bidders," Kostadinovic said.
"As soon as the law is adopted, the commission will call tenders and the best bidders will be chosen by the end of 1997," the minister added.
The Trans-Yugoslav highways project, planned to add another 1,200 kilometres to the existing road network over next five years, has already attracted some French and Greek interests.
"But there are at least five or six other foreign companies interested in the project," the minister said.
Foreigners can opt for a simple concession deal, joint venture or a deal with the government with sharing investment and profit. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
